chunks: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babuwayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-'Attar narrated to us. He said: Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami narrated to us from Harun ibn Muslim, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Ali ibn Isma'il. He said: Abu Usama Zayd al-Shahham informed me. He said: I heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) saying:
Whoever delays Maghrib until the stars come out without a reason, then I dissociate from him before God.

key_terms.المغرب: Maghrib - the sunset prayer, one of the five obligatory daily prayers, performed shortly after sunset
key_terms.بريء: free/dissociated - expressing the Imam's disavowal of such behavior
key_terms.تشتبك النجوم: the stars become intertwined - an Arabic idiom meaning the sky fills with stars, indicating it is well past sunset
key_terms.علة: a legitimate reason or excuse that would justify delaying the prayer

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about delaying the Maghrib prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issued a stern warning against delaying the Maghrib (sunset) prayer beyond its proper time without a legitimate excuse. The expression "until the stars become intertwined" (i.e., until the sky is full of stars) indicates significant delay past sunset. This teaching was addressed to the Shia community during the Imam's time, emphasizing that punctuality in prayer is so important that the Imam himself dissociates from those who neglect it.
